memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After Abram returned from defeating Kedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, the king of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (that is, the King's Valley). - Gen 14:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram comes home victorious, and immediately two kings come out to meet him. First the king of Sodom, then Melchizedek, king of Salem. Two kings, two encounters, two very different offers - and Abram's response to each will reveal his heart.

The king of Sodom represents the world's approach: he will come with a deal, an offer of wealth, a transaction. Melchizedek will come with bread and wine and a blessing from God Most High. One offers what Abram can take; the other gives what Abram can only receive.

Notice the timing. This meeting comes right after Abram's greatest victory. That is often when we are most vulnerable. Success opens the door to offers we would have refused in humbler times. The moment of triumph is the moment temptation comes calling.

We face the same two kings, in a sense - the world's offer and God's gift. One flatters us, buys us, makes us feel important. The other blesses us freely and asks us to receive. Jesus warned that "no one can serve two masters" (Matt 6:24). After every victory, watch carefully who comes out to meet you, and be sure which king you belong to.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you more vulnerable to compromise after success than after failure?
- Which "king" has your allegiance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, guard my heart in the moments of success, when temptation comes dressed as opportunity. Help me know which king I serve, and give me discernment about every offer that comes my way.
Amen.
